Drop the no-row exemption for profiles, let profileConflict keepLocal insert the row when it is missing (as epicConflict keepLocal does), and flip the finalizer test that asserts the overwrite (finalizer.test.ts about :983-996). discoveries.body: exportRunHistory and exportProfile have no restoreFile and no export intent, unlike exportEpic. A read-back failure, a recordExport error or a kill before commit leaves this machine's own new file with no sync record; after a further change the next flush refuses it as another machine's and the card offers a choice about this machine's own write, where Keep tracked restores older values. Restore the previous text on failure and record an intent so an interrupted export is recognized as this machine's. Red-team repro: /tmp/dm-redteam/redteam.test.ts (case 2).

discoveries.body: planRuns and scanProfiles plan only records they could read, so a pulled run.json or profile the reconcile rejects (for example over the 8 MiB record limit, which this machine's own exports may exceed) gets no conflict row: every flush is refused and the Storage card offers nothing, although resolveRecordConflict local would work. For each rejected run or profile with a waiting export and an unimported tracked file, record a conflict (run conflicts under the run's local epic id) so Write local is offered and Keep tracked refuses with the rejection reason. Red-team repro: /tmp/dm-redteam/redteam2.test.ts.
discoveries.title: Record a conflict for a rejected pulled run or profile whose export waits

discoveries.body: Keep tracked imports the tracked run but leaves rows the file lacks (such as this machine's claimed attempt) in the database; for a finished run nothing exports them again, so this machine's view diverges, against runConflict.ts's own doc. Decide and implement: drop those rows inside the Keep tracked transaction, or queue the run's export so they go out, and make the doc and the card or toast text say what happens. Also update the resolveRecordConflict doc in shared/domain/api.ts and the comment in core/authz.ts, which name only epics and runs. Found by the red-team and by DM-364.

content.summary:
Sprint 1 delivered all seven follow-ups and its acceptance passed once on the combined work (8,738 tests; coverage 97.74% lines, 95.05% branches), landed as a9b0cea on linear-followups. A run's history and a profile are no longer written over another machine's unimported copy once this machine has a sync record for it, and the person chooses Keep tracked records or Write local in the Storage card (one person-only resolveRecordConflict command). An epic imports while its run's history waits, stale reconcile conflicts clear, an oversized Linear transfer is refused at queue, the MCP transport wiring is tested, and start errors keep their last letters. An independent red-team after acceptance found that a new local profile can still overwrite a pulled profile of the same name before the first reconcile creates its sync record (the plan's own 'missing row writes' exemption), plus three minor gaps. Success criterion s1 is therefore not met yet; the redraft adds a Sprint 2 that closes all four.

Revision 2, after plan revision 2 was adopted: the epic-completion criterion (each success criterion holds) moved to Sprint 2, which closes the red-team's findings in DM-373 to DM-376. Sprint 1 is no longer the final sprint, so this report carries no epic outcome.
